steps.es: Sie müssen das Wasser nicht kaufen. Dort ist ein Brunnen.
steps.en: You do not have to buy water. There is a fountain over there.

options.feedback: The obvious question, and asking it is how you stop buying water for good.
She has just saved you two francs a day. Take it.

options.es: Das Wasser im Brunnen? Nein, merci.
options.en: The water in the fountain? No, thanks.
options.feedback: She is not offering you puddle water. Almost every fountain in the country runs drinking water.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Natürlich. Fast alle Brunnen sind Trinkwasser.
steps.en: Of course. Almost all the fountains are drinking water.

options.feedback: Exactly the right follow-up. There is a sign, and it says kein Trinkwasser.
Go and fill the bottle you already paid for. That is the whole trick.

options.es: In der Stadt? Das ist nicht sauber.
options.en: In town? That is not clean.
options.feedback: It comes off the mountain and it is colder and cleaner than the bottle in your hand.

steps.speaker: Die alte Frau
steps.es: Das macht jeder am Anfang. Ade.
steps.en: Everybody does that at the start. Goodbye.

options.feedback: She told you something useful and did not make you feel stupid. That deserves the full merci vielmal.
Correct, and it skips the thank you she had earned.

options.en: I am not at the start.
options.feedback: You are, and she was being kind about it.

scenarios.title: Am Samstagabend
scenarios.desc: The shop shut two hours ago
scenarios.setting: Half past six on a Saturday, no milk in the flat, and everything dark.

steps.speaker: Ein Mann vor dem Laden
steps.es: Der ist schon zu. Seit fünf.
steps.en: It has been shut since five.

options.feedback: Say the thing you cannot believe. He will explain it, because everybody here has had this conversation.
Fine, and it ends the conversation before he tells you the useful part.

options.es: Aber es ist erst halb sieben.
options.en: But it is only half past six.
options.feedback: It is, and the shop shut at five regardless. Arguing with the opening hours is a beginner move.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Am Samstag schliessen die Läden früh. Und am Sonntag ist alles zu.
steps.en: On Saturday the shops close early. And on Sunday everything is shut.

options.feedback: Yes. This is the single most useful fact anybody will tell you in your first month.
Sometimes it opens for an hour or two in the morning. That is the whole exception, apart from the station.

options.es: Das ist nicht gut für den Laden.
options.en: That is not good for the shop.
options.feedback: Everybody here has decided otherwise, repeatedly, at the ballot box.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Am Bahnhof ist etwas offen. Auch am Sonntag.
steps.en: There is something open at the station. On Sunday too.

options.en: At the station? Thanks very much!
options.feedback: The station shops are the exception the whole country runs on. Now you know it too.
Yes. And it is open, which on a Sunday is the only thing that matters.
It is a fifteen minute walk and the alternative is no milk until Monday.

steps.speaker: Der Mann
steps.es: Nächstes Mal am Freitag einkaufen. Ade.
steps.en: Do your shopping on Friday next time. Goodbye.

options.en: Thanks. I will do that. Goodbye.
options.feedback: You will, and by the third weekend it will not be a decision any more.
He gave you the rule and the exception in under a minute. Worth the vielmal.
He stopped in the street to save you a wasted Sunday.

scenarios.title: Die Schlüsselübergabe
scenarios.desc: Three keys and a great deal of information
scenarios.setting: Two o’clock, an empty flat, and a landlord who says everything twice.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Grüezi. Also, das ist die Wohnung.
steps.en: Grüezi. So, this is the flat.

options.feedback: His name back to him. Nobody here minds being called by it, and using it says you were listening.
Fine. Merci is the word you will hear back from him.
It is empty because it was handed over cleaned to the corner, which is what he is about to explain.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Der erste Schlüssel ist für die Wohnung, der zweite für das Haus.
steps.en: The first key is for the flat, the second for the building.

options.feedback: There is always a third and it is always the cellar. Asking is quicker than being told twice.
He will say it again anyway. He says everything twice.
You do. The cellar is where your bike is going to live.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Nach dem Duschen müssen Sie das Fenster aufmachen. Sonst gibt es Schimmel.
steps.en: After showering you have to open the window. Otherwise you get mould.

options.feedback: Short and it is a promise. Mould at the handover comes out of your deposit.
Especially in winter. Asking shows you took it as a rule and not as small talk.
He will let that pass and he will remember it.

steps.speaker: Herr Kaufmann
steps.es: Die Miete müssen Sie bis am dritten bezahlen. Nicht am vierten.
steps.en: You have to pay the rent by the third. Not the fourth.

options.es: Bis am dritten. Ich schreibe es auf.
options.en: By the third. I will write it down.
options.feedback: He said a date and a not-date. Repeating the date back is the whole answer.
True, and it does not show him you registered which day.
Then a Mahnung comes, it costs twenty francs, and you have just told your landlord you might.

scenarios.title: Am Dienstag gewaschen
scenarios.desc: You used the machine on somebody else’s day
scenarios.setting: The laundry room, two hours later, with your washing still in the machine.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Entschuldigung. Der Dienstag ist mein Tag.
steps.en: Excuse me. Tuesday is my day.

options.feedback: She is right, and saying so ends it. Nobody here wants an argument, they want the rota kept.

options.es: Die Maschine ist leer. Ich dachte, es geht.
options.en: The machine was empty. I thought it was fine.
options.feedback: A reason, which she will accept and not agree with. Empty is not the same as free.

options.en: But nobody is using it right now.
options.feedback: That is the argument, and it is the one that makes an enemy in a building you will live in for years.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Sie müssen sich in den Plan eintragen. Dann gehört der Tag Ihnen.
steps.en: You have to sign into the rota. Then the day is yours.

options.es: Ich trage mich das nächste Mal ein.
options.en: I will sign myself in next time.
options.feedback: Uses her own verb back. eintragen is the word the whole system runs on.
On the wall by the door. Asking is better than guessing again.
Yes, and it is in the Hausordnung, which she knows and now knows you have not read.

steps.speaker: Frau Steiner
steps.es: Nehmen Sie Ihre Wäsche heraus. Ich brauche die Maschine jetzt.
steps.en: Take your washing out. I need the machine now.

options.feedback: Immediate and one more apology. That closes it properly.
The Tumbler is Tuesday’s too. You are asking for the second half of the day you already took.
Reasonable, and she has been waiting two hours already.

steps.speaker: Frau Amrein
steps.es: Und? War die Frau Steiner böse?

options.feedback: The right answer, and she will report it to the building exactly as you said it.
Honest. She will tell you Frau Steiner is never cross, which is nearly true.

options.en: How do you know about it already?
options.feedback: She always knows already. Asking her that is a joke she will enjoy.

scenarios.title: Beim Hauswart
scenarios.desc: Reporting a problem, in the one hour he is there
scenarios.setting: Five o’clock, the ground floor, and a bathroom light that stopped working yesterday.

options.es: Grüezi. Das Licht im Bad ist kaputt.
options.en: Grüezi. The bathroom light is broken.
options.feedback: Greeting and then the problem in one short sentence. He is waiting for exactly that and nothing else.

options.en: Grüezi. Do you have a moment?
options.feedback: Polite, and it makes him ask what for. He would rather you just said it.
Not unfriendly, just not what this hour is for. He will wait for the actual reason.
Two words. He is already writing it in the book.

options.en: The flat next to Frau Amrein.
options.feedback: He knows exactly which one that is. The number is faster.

options.es: Ich wohne seit einem Monat hier.
options.en: I have been living here a month.
options.feedback: Not the question. He asked which flat.
He will be there at eight. Not five past. Take the time and say thank you.
It could, and you have just made work out of something that was finished.

options.es: Können Sie es heute noch machen?
options.en: Could you still do it today?
options.feedback: You report a problem to him. You do not set his schedule.

options.en: Thanks very much. That was quick.
options.feedback: Four minutes. Noticing it out loud is the closest thing to a compliment he will accept.
Fine. He will nod and pack up.
He will tell you in about six words. It is a fair question.

scenarios.title: Bei der Gemeinde
scenarios.desc: Registering, in eleven minutes
scenarios.setting: Eight in the morning, ticket B twelve, and a folder with four documents in it.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: Grüezi. Was kann ich für Sie tun?
steps.en: Grüezi. What can I do for you?

options.en: Grüezi. I would like to register.
options.feedback: The exact sentence for the exact counter. He will have the form out before you finish it.
True, and he still has to ask what you want. anmelden is the word.

options.en: Grüezi. I need a bank account.
options.feedback: Wrong building. But you do need this first, and the bank will ask for what he is about to give you.
bitte handing something over is one of the four jobs that word does.
It is. Asking costs nothing.
Then this is a second trip. Bring everything, every time.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: Und die Religion? Sie müssen das nicht ausfüllen.
steps.en: And religion? You do not have to fill that in.

options.feedback: Because the church is funded by tax here. He will tell you plainly and it is worth knowing.

options.en: Then I will leave it empty.
options.feedback: He told you it was optional. Taking him at his word is fine.

options.en: Do I have to fill that in?
options.feedback: He has just said you do not. Worth listening to the second half of the sentence.

steps.speaker: Der Beamte
steps.es: So. Das ist die Bestätigung. Willkommen in Luzern.
steps.en: There. That is your confirmation. Welcome to Luzern.

options.feedback: He meant the welcome. It is said without ceremony and it is not nothing.
For the bank and for the insurer. Do not lose it, which is what he is about to say.
It is. Eleven minutes, which will keep surprising you.

scenarios.title: Der Nachbar an der Tür
scenarios.desc: He came up two floors in his socks
scenarios.setting: Three in the afternoon. You have just dragged a table across a wooden floor twice.

steps.speaker: Herr Bucher
steps.es: Grüezi. Ich bin Bucher, von unten.
steps.en: Grüezi. I am Bucher, from downstairs.

options.feedback: You know why he is here and you say so first. That is the whole conversation over in one line.

options.es: Grüezi. Was kann ich für Sie tun?
options.en: Grüezi. What can I do for you?
options.feedback: Polite, and it makes him say the awkward part out loud.

options.es: Grüezi. Es ist erst drei Uhr.
options.en: Grüezi. It is only three o’clock.
options.feedback: It is, and he works at home, which he has not told you yet because you did not let him.

options.en: I did not know that. Sorry.
options.feedback: He is not complaining, he is telling you a fact you needed. Take it that way.

options.en: I will not move anything else.
options.feedback: Concrete, and it is the thing he actually wants.
Yes. And now you know why the building is silent at eleven in the morning.

options.es: Nein. Aber ich kann einen kaufen.
options.en: No. But I can buy one.
options.feedback: That is the answer he came up two floors for, and he did not have to ask for it.
It does, a lot, and asking makes it his suggestion rather than your concession.
He would not have mentioned it otherwise.

options.es: Grüezi, Herr Bucher. Gut, merci. Und Ihnen?
options.en: Grüezi, Herr Bucher. Good, thanks. And you?
options.feedback: Two weeks and a rug later, he is asking. That is not a small thing here — answer it properly and ask back.
Correct and it leaves his question half answered. The Und Ihnen is the other half.
The everyday answer, and it lands as easy rather than formal. He will use it back at you.

scenarios.title: Bei Nuno
scenarios.desc: Friday at seven, and he does come at seven
scenarios.setting: A kitchen after service, a bottle of something, and the first person here who talks fast.

options.feedback: Hoi back, not Grüezi. He offered du and the informal greeting in one word, and taking it is the answer.
Not wrong, and it is a step more formal than what he just gave you. He will not mind and he will notice.
The other informal one. Same register, and it is what you would hear around Zurich and the centre.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Und? Wie ist der erste Monat?
steps.en: Well? How is the first month?

options.feedback: Two words and he will laugh, because it is exactly right and he remembers it.
Honest, and it opens the conversation he wants to have.
True, and it is the thing every newcomer says first. He has heard it eighteen years running.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Lern die Artikel jetzt. Sofort. Nicht später.
steps.en: Learn the articles now. Straight away. Not later.

options.es: Der Tisch, die Wohnung, das Bad.
options.en: Der Tisch, die Wohnung, das Bad.
options.feedback: You did not agree, you demonstrated. That is the only answer he wanted.
They do. And everybody hears it, which is what he is trying to tell you.
This is the one piece of advice he gives everybody, because nobody gave it to him.

steps.speaker: Nuno
steps.es: Die Fehler sind nicht das Problem. Das Schweigen ist das Problem.
steps.en: The mistakes are not the problem. The silence is the problem.

options.feedback: You do. Forty minutes at an airport without saying a word taught you the same thing.

options.es: Zwei Jahre still. Das ist lang.
options.en: Two years silent. That is a long time.
options.feedback: It is, and he said it about himself. Repeating it back shows you heard which part mattered.

options.es: Ich habe keine Angst vor Fehlern.
options.en: I am not afraid of mistakes.
options.feedback: Everybody says that in the first month. He will simply keep talking to you and find out.

scenarios.title: Das Übliche?
scenarios.desc: Somebody starts your coffee before you get there
scenarios.setting: Quarter past seven, the machine already running, and a question that is not really a question.

options.feedback: Two words, and the second one carries all of it. Gern is how enthusiasm is said here.
You gave her the word back. That is exactly what a regular does with it.
Fair, the first time. But she has watched you order the same thing forty mornings running.
Three words and it is true. She has heard it from everybody who arrives, and she asks anyway.
Correct and closed. One sentence more is what turns this into a conversation.
A closed door. Ja on its own ends it, and she was opening something.
You do. And agreeing with a small direct observation is the whole answer here.

options.en: I do not have much time.
options.feedback: True, and she will point out that the coffee costs the same sitting down.
She has watched you do it for a month. This is a correction and it is meant kindly.
You said it back. Ade is for a guest, bis morgen is for somebody who is coming back.
Not wrong, and it is the more distant of the two. She just gave you the closer one.
You will be there at quarter past seven and both of you know it.

scenarios.title: Vier Minuten
scenarios.desc: The bus is late and somebody looks at the sky
scenarios.setting: A bus stop, rain on the shelter, and a woman with a very old dog.

options.es: Ja. Gestern hat es den ganzen Tag geregnet.
options.en: Yes. Yesterday it rained all day.
options.feedback: Yes plus one sentence. The weather is the door, and you walked through it.
Polite and finished. She will not push, and nothing more will happen.
She knows. She was not making a claim about the weather, she was asking whether you want to talk.
A small failure of your own, offered up. It is the fastest way past the weather.
True and short. She has one too, and she left it on the bus.
Not a mistake. But every no here can carry a second sentence and this one does not.
Seit takes the dative, and this is the answer everybody gives. You will say it a hundred times.
Seit einem. The dative is not optional here and it is the commonest slip in the first year.
Fine. Her next question was going to be how long, so you can save her the trouble.

options.en: I like the town very much.
options.feedback: Gefallen puts the thing in charge: it pleases me. The person goes in the dative and stays there.
Backwards, and it says something else entirely. The town does the pleasing, not you.
Warm enough. Name the thing you like and she will tell you where to sit in spring.

scenarios.title: Woher kommst du?
scenarios.desc: The question you will answer a thousand times
scenarios.setting: An apéro, a glass in your hand, and a man who has asked this before.

options.es: Aus dem Süden. Aus einer kleinen Stadt.
options.en: From the south. From a small town.
options.feedback: The place, then the country. Here the part matters more than the nation, and he will ask which part anyway.
No edge is meant. He asks a man from Bern the same thing and hears it in the vowels.
Charming and it dodges. He will simply ask again, more slowly.

steps.speaker: Marco
steps.es: Und seit wann sind Sie hier?
steps.en: And since when have you been here?

options.feedback: Seit einem Monat, seit einer Woche, seit einem Jahr. Nuno still gets asked after eighteen years.
Understood, and it drops the word that carries the sense. Seit is what makes it a stretch of time.
That is the day you arrived. Seit is the whole month since, and he asked for the month.

options.es: Ich arbeite in einem Büro. Zahlen und Briefe.
options.en: I work in an office. Numbers and letters.
options.feedback: Plain, and plain is the register. Nobody will ask what you earn, and nobody thinks less of the answer.
He asked what you trained as, which here usually means an apprenticeship. Two of three people did one.
Money does not come into this conversation. It will not come into any of them.

steps.speaker: Marco
steps.es: Mein Bruder wohnt auch im Süden.
steps.en: My brother lives in the south too.

options.feedback: You asked back. He has been waiting for somebody to, and now you will hear about the brother.
He opened a door with his own family in it. One question is all it needed.
He gave you something personal. Ja hands it straight back unopened.

scenarios.title: Zum Wohl
scenarios.desc: Eight people, eight glasses, and one rule
scenarios.setting: Half past five, everybody standing, and a plate of olives nobody is eating from.

steps.speaker: Petra
steps.en: Would you like a glass of wine?

options.feedback: Gern does the work, and naming what you want saves a second question.

options.en: No, thank you. A water, please.
options.feedback: Nobody asks twice and nobody minds. A water is a glass, and a glass is all this needs.
She will pour you something. But the offer was a small question with a small answer.
The name, and her eyes, and only then the glass. All three or it does not count.
Half of it. The name is not decoration here, it is the part people notice is missing.
Heard here too, and it is the louder one. Zum Wohl is what an apéro in Luzern mostly says, and it is what she just said.

options.es: Nein. Ich habe gedacht, es gibt Abendessen.
options.en: No. I thought there would be dinner.
options.feedback: Every newcomer makes this mistake once. An apéro is a glass and four olives, and it ends at seven.
Then somebody told you, or you learned it the hard way. Either way you are ahead.
Three olives and four nuts. Not half the plate, which is what hunger does to a newcomer.
It is seven, and at seven everybody puts the glass down at the same moment with no signal at all.
It is early. It is also over, and that is the shape of the thing rather than a judgement on it.
An apéro has an end time the way it has a start time. Asking her to stay puts her in an awkward spot.

scenarios.title: Wollen wir du sagen?
scenarios.desc: A cake, a first name, and a small ceremony
scenarios.setting: Sunday afternoon, your own doorway, and the woman who has said Sie for five weeks.

options.feedback: And then your own first name back. That is the whole ceremony: two first names and a handshake.
You missed it. She gave you her first name after five weeks of not giving it.
You knew the name. She was not telling you the name, she was offering you the du.
The offer comes from the older person and it comes once. Yes is very nearly the only answer.
Still on Sie in the sentence that agrees to leave it. She will laugh, and she will not mind.
Possible, and it is a real refusal of something she thought about for five weeks first.
Dir, not Ihnen. The mouth takes about three weeks to catch up and she has already said so.
The slip everybody makes. She will just say her first name again and wait.
Honest and small, which is the register. Es geht is a real answer here and not a complaint.
Du and the first name in one sentence. That is the pairing, and it is the part that takes practice.
Du and Frau Amrein do not go together. Pick one register and this one is already picked.

options.es: Nein, danke. Ich mache uns einen.
options.en: No, thank you. I will make us one.
options.feedback: Better than accepting. She came across the landing with a cake and you can cross it back.

scenarios.title: Am Tisch
scenarios.desc: Three hours, one small pan, and no hurry at all
scenarios.setting: A flat the same shape as yours, forty years older, and an oven in the middle of the table.

options.feedback: Short is right. This is the first time you have been past her door and neither of you will mention that.
There are two chairs. One of them is hers and has been for forty years.
Setz dich is an instruction shaped like an offer. Raclette is a table you sit at.
Gib mir: the person in the dative, the thing in the accusative. It is the shape of half this evening.

options.en: I am giving you the cheese.
options.feedback: Dir and den. Both cases in one short sentence, and you built it right.
Dir. The person receiving always sits in the dative, with geben, zeigen, schicken and schenken alike.
Fein is for food. Gut is for work and for weather, and using it here marks you out at once.
Understood, and it is the word for a job well done rather than for a plate.
She has made this for you for three hours. Es geht is what you say about a bus.

steps.speaker: Rosmarie
steps.en: Do not drink anything cold with it.

options.en: Then I will have a tea.
options.feedback: Tea or white wine. Whether the rule is true is beside the point: her mother said it.
You will get the explanation, and the explanation is that her mother said so. It is enough.
It may not be. It is also her table, her cheese, and a thing she has believed for seventy years.

scenarios.title: Am Samstag?
scenarios.desc: An invitation with a date in it, and one without
scenarios.setting: After the club, a car park, and somebody deciding how much to commit to.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.en: We should eat together some time.

options.es: Gern. Hast du am Freitag Zeit?
options.en: Gladly. Are you free on Friday?
options.feedback: You turned mal into a date. That is the whole move, and it is the one nobody expects you to make.
Warm and it commits nobody. Mal has no date in it, so nothing will happen unless somebody adds one.
Fair question, and a slightly hard one. Naming a day yourself is easier for both of you.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Freitag geht nicht. Der Dienstag danach?
steps.en: Friday does not work. The Tuesday after?

options.feedback: Settled, and nobody will mention it again until Tuesday. That is what an arrangement is here.
Maybe is not an answer to a date. Say yes or say no and either one is fine.

options.es: Ich schaue noch. Ich sage dir Bescheid.
options.en: I will see. I will let you know.
options.feedback: Honest, and it puts the work on him. He got his calendar out of his bag for this.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Kommst du am Samstag ans Spiel?
steps.en: Are you coming to the match on Saturday?

options.es: Ja, gern. Um wie viel Uhr?
options.feedback: Yes and then the practical question. Both halves, in that order.

options.es: Ich habe leider schon etwas abgemacht.
options.en: Unfortunately I have already arranged something.
options.feedback: Leider, and no reason. Nobody asks what, and the reason stays yours.
It is Wednesday. By local arithmetic three days out is practically the day itself.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Also am Dienstag um halb acht.
steps.en: So Tuesday at half past seven.

options.es: Ich bin um zwanzig nach da.
options.en: I will be there at twenty past.
options.feedback: Five minutes early is on time. Saying so out loud is not fussy here, it is normal.
Done. He will be outside at twenty-five past and so, now, will you.
Half past seven is half past seven. Roughly is what the message four minutes beforehand is for.

scenarios.title: In der Gruppe
scenarios.desc: Fourteen people, eighty messages, and one thumb
scenarios.setting: Your phone on the table at nine in the evening, going off every forty seconds.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Samstag Grillieren bei mir. Wer kommt?
steps.en: Barbecue at my place on Saturday. Who is coming?

options.en: I will be there. At seven?
options.feedback: Short, and it drops the ich. That is the register for messages and a long sentence reads as a problem.

options.es: Ich komme sehr gern und freue mich schon.
options.en: I am coming very gladly and am already looking forward to it.
options.feedback: Nothing is wrong with it. It is four times longer than every other reply and he will ask if you are all right.
A thumb is a yes. Not I have read this: I am coming. People have been counted absent for the difference.
Two words and it is binding. Nobody will ask again, and the bread had better be there.
Now nobody knows whether there is bread. In a group of fourteen, maybe is worse than no.
Fine. Ask in the group rather than to him alone, and somebody will name a thing.
He is seventy-one, he sends the same picture of flowers every morning at six, and nobody answers. Nobody minds either.
Kind, and now there are two messages where the group expected none. He will be pleased.

options.en: It is six in the morning.
options.feedback: It is. He has been up since half past four and this is what he does with the hour.

steps.speaker: Timo
steps.es: Du warst nicht da. Alles gut?
steps.en: You were not there. Everything all right?

options.es: Es tut mir leid. Ich habe nur den Daumen geschickt.
options.en: I am sorry. I only sent the thumb.
options.feedback: Said on the same day it is nothing. Left for three days it becomes a thing, and Nuno will tell you so.
You sent a thumb. Here that is the yes, and the argument will not go your way.
Fine as far as it goes. Sending that on Friday instead of explaining it on Wednesday is the fix.

kennen.en: to know a person or place

phrases.en: I only speak a little German.

phrases.es: Bitte langsam. Ich verstehe nicht alles.
phrases.en: Slowly, please. I do not understand everything.

phrases.es: 1414 ist die Rega, die Rettung aus der Luft.
phrases.en: 1414 is the Rega, the air rescue.

emergency.title: If you are hurt or ill

phrases.es: Man hat mir das Portemonnaie gestohlen.
Ich habe den letzten Zug verpasst.
phrases.en: I have missed the last train.

phrases.es: Ich weiss nicht, wo ich bin.
phrases.en: I do not know where I am.
